faq: Will my store be offline during the switch?

Not in most cases. We prepare everything on the new store first and change the domain records at a quiet time. Some visitors may see the old site for a few hours while the change spreads across the internet.
Do I need to own the domain?

Yes, and we need access to the domain settings at your registrar, such as GoDaddy or Namecheap. We guide you through adding the right records yourself, or you can add us as a delegate if the registrar allows it.
What if something goes wrong at launch?
Premium includes a rollback plan that points the domain back to the old store within minutes. For other packages we pause and fix, or reverse the change together, and then agree a new time.
Can you handle a launch on a weekend?
We plan the launch time with you, including evenings and weekends, and confirm it before you order. Launch support for a specific day is booked when the order is placed.

desc:
Store go-live and domain switch support means having a person plan and watch the day your new store replaces the old one. Ecom Swift LLC manages the domain change, checks orders and emails, and stays on hand through the first hours of your launch.

## What is go-live support?

Go-live support is hands-on help during the switch from your old store to your new one. The key step is pointing your domain name at the new store, so that visitors who type your address reach the new site. Around that step sit checks: does the site load securely, can a customer pay, do emails arrive, do old links still work.

The domain change is small, but the surrounding details are where launches go wrong.

## Why launch day needs a plan

Until the switch, nobody sees the new store but you. After it, every mistake is public. A missing certificate shows a browser warning. A wrong shipping rate charges real customers. An email setting that was never tested can leave order confirmations in spam folders.

Domain changes also take time to spread across the internet, because records are cached by providers. If nobody prepares for that, some visitors see the old store while others see the new one, and orders land in two places. Planning the timing and the cache settings in advance keeps the changeover tidy.

## How a calm launch protects revenue

Launch is often tied to a sale, a season or an email campaign. If the site breaks during that window, you lose orders you cannot get back and spend the next days answering worried messages. Having someone watch the first hours means problems are caught while the traffic is still small.

It also reduces stress for the owner. You know what will happen, at what time, and who is checking each part. If something does go wrong, there is a clear route to reverse the change rather than a scramble.

## What strong launch support includes

- A written launch plan with an agreed date and time.
- The domain's cache time lowered ahead of the switch so changes spread faster.
- Domain records updated together with you, using your own registrar or host account.
- HTTPS and the security certificate confirmed on the live address.
- A first real order placed and followed to confirmation.
- Checks of order emails and domain email, including sending and receiving.
- Redirect tests from old links to new pages.
- Monitoring of orders and error messages during the first hours.
- A rollback plan, in the larger package, that lets you point back to the old store if needed.
- A launch log recording what was changed and when.

## What we do

Before launch we agree a time that suits your traffic and your calendar. We review the checklist with you, confirm that the new store is ready and prepare the domain settings. If you want a freeze on the old store, we agree it so that no new orders or product edits are lost.

At the agreed time we make the changes with you, or guide you through them if your registrar needs you to click. We then work through the checks: the store loads, the certificate is valid, a test order goes through, emails are sent. In higher packages we keep watching for several days and prepare a short note for your customers.

Afterwards you receive the launch log and a short list of things to look at in the first week.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Pick a quiet time, not the middle of a sale.
- Confirm you control the domain account before the day.
- Keep the old store running until the new one is proven.
- Tell your team the time of the switch.
- Place a real order yourself once the store is live.

**Avoid:**
- Changing products or prices on the old store during the switch.
- Launching late on a day when nobody can respond.
- Deleting the old site on the same day.
- Forgetting email records attached to the domain.
- Skipping the check of the certificate.

## Who this is for

An owner moving a busy store who cannot afford a bad launch. A first-time migrator who has never changed domain records and wants someone alongside. A team that has built the new store and now needs a reliable plan for the final step.

## How to get started

Send us the domain name, where it is registered and the date you have in mind. We need to work out who holds the login for the registrar, and we ask you to make the record changes yourself or add us as a delegated user if your provider offers that.

We never need your passwords. If a provider does not support extra users, we give you the exact values to enter and check the result together.
